defects.title: test_generate_fallback_relaxed_tree_still_avoids_an_active_ban_set is vacuous — deleting the _ban_ok check it claims to pin leaves all 27 tests green
defects.failure_scenario: The test's own docstring says "`relaxed` must still track only a tree that is ban_ok (not just any minimal collapse), proving the fallback discriminates on the ban set and not merely on is_valid_root". Delete `self._ban_ok(tree) and` from generator.py:248 (leaving `if relaxed is None and is_valid_root(tree)`) and run `pytest tests/test_generator_hooks.py`: 27 passed. Reproduced with /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP5/mutate.py (MUT=M1_relaxed_no_ban) and again standalone in a4_fake_test.py. The reason it cannot fail: it bans exactly ONE of the ~320 minimal keys the fallback can draw (`victim = next(iter(one_layer_keys(probe._collapse_leaf(pool[0]))))`), so P(first fallback draw is the victim) ~ 0.3% — with seed 2 the un-checked version returns `O:day_durbin_watson(F:Ret)`, which satisfies both assertions. The check is genuinely load-bearing: banning 319 of the 320 reachable minimal keys with an always-False hook, the un-checked version returns a BANNED tree in 40/40 seeds while the shipped code leaks 0/40 (28 raise GenerationExhausted, 12 return the one spare). So the central correctness property of the WP5 fix — the design's deliberate behaviour change (b), "a fallback tree carrying a banned key is no longer returned" — has no test at all, and a future refactor of generate() can reintroduce the leak silently.
defects.suggested_fix: Make the ban set cover the draws. Enumerate the reachable minimal keys once (`keys = set(); for s in probe._root_ops_of('reduce'): for _ in range(400): keys |= one_layer_keys(probe._collapse_leaf(s))` — 320 of them), ban `keys - {spare}` for one chosen `spare`, install `accept=lambda t: False`, and over ~20 seeds assert that `generate()` either raises GenerationExhausted or returns a tree whose one_layer_keys are disjoint from the ban set — never a banned one. Keep the existing single-victim case as a cheap smoke test if desired, but it must not be the thing the docstring's claim rests on.

defects.title: _pick_weighted's face mass divides by the face's full operator count, not by the surviving (weight>0) count, so it does not reproduce Partura's pick
defects.failure_scenario: The design states the semantics normatively twice — §"2. Generator": "a face's mass is its operators' mean weight ... which reproduces Partura's current `pick` exactly, so the migration changes no behaviour" and "Weight 0 is how 'drop this operator from the vocabulary without shifting the draws' is expressed"; WP5 step 7: "This reproduces Partura's current pick semantics exactly, so the migration is behaviour-preserving". Partura's actual pick (/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/scripts/idea_search.py:225-238) filters `if w > 0` BEFORE building the face lists, so `sum(w)/len(faces[n])` divides by the number of SURVIVING operators. The shipped `masses = [sum(weights[face]) / len(weights[face]) ...]` divides by the number of ALL operators in the face, so a face's probability is scaled by its surviving fraction. Measured (a3_partura_pick.py, a6_real_weights.py): zeroing the 55 dt/in operators gives P(dt face) = 0.1404 empirically (0.1406 analytic) under the shipped code vs 0.2485 (0.2500 analytic) under Partura's pick and 0.25 under the uniform path — a 1.8x distortion; with only `day_mean` surviving in dt, 0.0031 vs 0.25 — 81x. Partura runs with allow_resource_risk=True (idea_search.py:321) and `base_weight` zeroes the resource_risk ops in BOTH arms, and the steer arm's `operator_weights()` (partura/steer.py:395) assigns 0.0 for every generic `ban` rule, so the shift is proportional to how many operators a steer config bans per face — and the `shared` face has only 17 members. Consequence: WP11's migration silently changes both arms' operator distribution instead of preserving it, and weight 0 does shift the draws. No test catches it: replacing the mean with a plain sum (MUT=M4_face_mass_sum) leaves all 27 tests green, i.e. nothing pins face-balancing in the weighted path at all.
defects.suggested_fix:
Drop the zero-weight specs from the face before taking the mean, exactly as Partura does, keeping the same two `choices` draws:
```python
live_specs = {f: [(s, w) for s, w in zip(faces[f], weights[f]) if w > 0.0] for f in faces}
live = [f for f in sorted(faces) if live_specs[f]]
if not live:
    return self._rng.choice(faces[self._rng.choice(sorted(faces))])
masses = [sum(w for _, w in live_specs[f]) / len(live_specs[f]) for f in live]
face = self._rng.choices(live, weights=masses)[0]
return self._rng.choices([s for s, _ in live_specs[face]], weights=[w for _, w in live_specs[face]])[0]
```
Add the two missing tests: (1) `op_weight=lambda s: 1.0` must give the same face-share distribution as `op_weight=None` over ~100k draws (this is what kills the sum-instead-of-mean mutation); (2) zeroing most of one face must leave that face's share at its uniform value, not at its surviving fraction.

defects.title: hook_rng is random.Random(0) in every mining run, because gp.py constructs the generator with rng= and never seed=
defects.failure_scenario: `self.hook_rng = random.Random((seed * 2654435761) & 0xFFFFFFFF)` reads the `seed` keyword, but the only in-tree construction site — gp.py:241, `TypedTreeGenerator(registry, fields=..., n_minutes=..., min_depth=..., max_depth=..., allow_boolean_ops=..., allow_resource_risk=..., rng=self._rng)` — passes `rng=` and no `seed=`, so `seed` stays at its default 0 and the hook stream is `Random(0)` whatever the run's seed. WP7 step 2 says to forward op_weight/accept/daily_fields/daily_leaf_prob/leaf_slots "into the existing TypedTreeGenerator(...) call at line 241" and does not add `seed=`, so the shipped wiring is what WP7 will inherit. Measured (a7_hook_rng.py): GPMiner-style construction with run seeds 0, 7 and 12345 all yield hook_rng first draws [0.844422, 0.757954, 0.420572]; passing `seed=` instead gives three different streams. Two consequences: (a) the whole stated purpose — "an accept hook that needs a uniform draw must use it" so that "the steer/control comparison is reproducible from the seed" — fails in the direction nobody tests: varying the seed does not vary the hook's thinning draws at all, so N seeds of the steer arm share one thinning realisation, and Partura's current hook (idea_search.py:209, seeded from its own SEED) loses seed-dependence when it migrates to gen.hook_rng; (b) with the default seed=0, hook_rng and _rng are the SAME stream (verified: identical first three draws), contradicting the docstring's "a second, independent stream". test_hook_rng_is_a_distinct_deterministic_instance cannot see either problem — it only checks object identity and same-seed determinism.
defects.suggested_fix:
Derive the hook seed from the supplied rng when one is given; `getstate()` does not advance the stream, so this adds no draw and keeps the default path byte-identical:
```python
hook_seed = ((seed * 2654435761) & 0xFFFFFFFF) if rng is None else \
            (hash(rng.getstate()[1]) ^ 0x9E3779B9) & 0xFFFFFFFF
self.hook_rng = random.Random(hook_seed)
```
If WP5 must stay literal to the design text instead, then WP7 has to add `seed=seed` at gp.py:241 and that must be written into WP7's step list, because it is not there today. Either way add a test that two generators built the way gp.py builds them (`rng=random.Random(s)`, no seed=) with s=7 vs s=12345 get different hook_rng streams.

defects.title: on_exhausted is never validated, so a typo silently disables the strict mode
defects.failure_scenario: `self.on_exhausted = on_exhausted` stores the string unchecked and the only reader is `self.on_exhausted == "raise"`. Measured (a2_probes.py): `TypedTreeGenerator(..., accept=lambda t: False, on_exhausted="RAISE")` returns `O:day_quantile_q75(F:Open)` with unaccepted_fallbacks == 1 instead of raising; `on_exhausted="typo"` and `on_exhausted=None` behave the same. The design calls "raise" "the strict variant the correctness judge asked for" — a caller who wants a hard failure when the hook exhausts gets a silent relaxed tree instead, and the counter they would inspect looks like a normal fallback.
defects.suggested_fix: In __init__, next to the other construction-time checks: `if on_exhausted not in ("fallback", "raise"): raise ValueError(f"on_exhausted must be 'fallback' or 'raise', not {on_exhausted!r}")`, and store the validated value. Add it to the construction-rejection test block alongside the op_weight/accept cases.

defects.title: daily_fields and leaf_slots get no construction-time validation, unlike op_weight — misspellings fail late or as IndexError
defects.failure_scenario: op_weight mapping keys are checked against the registry at __init__ ("a typo'd name would otherwise sit silently inert"), but the two new daily-leaf keywords are stored raw. Measured (a2_probes.py, a5_edges.py): `daily_fields=("NotAFieldEither",), daily_leaf_prob=1.0` constructs fine and `_gen("daily", 1, full=False)` returns `DF:NotAFieldEither`, which can only fail later in WP4's leaf reader, i.e. mid-mining-run; `leaf_slots={"nope_xyz": {0: ("NotAField",)}}` is silently inert (the exact failure mode the op_weight check exists to prevent); `leaf_slots={"cs_regres": {7: ("FloatCap",)}}` silently ignores the out-of-range index; and `leaf_slots={"cs_regres": {1: ()}}` raises `IndexError: Cannot choose from an empty sequence` out of `_build` — not a ShapeError, so `_gen`'s `except ShapeError: continue` retry loop does not absorb it and it escapes `generate()`. WP7 step 6 adds exactly this kind of check for DF: ban keys against `registry.daily_fields`, so the registry already carries the information.
defects.suggested_fix: In __init__, after `self.daily_fields = list(daily_fields)`: reject any name not in `registry.daily_fields`. For leaf_slots, reject a key not in `registry` (`name not in registry`), a slot index that is negative or >= the spec's arity, any field name not in `registry.daily_fields`, and an empty field tuple — all ValueError naming the cause, matching the op_weight messages' shape. Extend test_leaf_slots_* with the rejection cases.

defects.title: A weight-0 operator can still be swapped in by mutate_operator via _pick_weighted's uniform fallback
defects.failure_scenario: `mutate_operator` narrows `alts` to one node's (category, arity, face, family) group. When every member of that group is weight 0, `_pick_weighted`'s `live` is empty and the uniform fallback draws from all of them, so a zero-weighted operator enters the child. Measured (a5_edges.py): with the 55 dt/in operators zeroed, 20 of 1200 mutate_operator children carried one, while 0 of 200 freshly generated trees did. The design sanctions the fallback ("a weight function must not be able to make generation impossible") and Partura's own pick has the identical `if not faces: return _pick(self, specs)`, so this is parity rather than a regression — but it means weight 0 is not an exclusion mechanism, and Partura zeroes the resource_risk operators for runtime reasons (idea_search.py:139/217 with allow_resource_risk=True), so a steer arm can still have a resource-risky kernel mutated into its population.
defects.suggested_fix: No code change is required for design conformance; if it should not happen, make the fallback narrow rather than global — when every weight in a given draw is 0, fall back to a uniform draw restricted to the specs that were passed in only if that is the whole vocabulary, and otherwise return None / let mutate_operator's retry loop pick another node. Minimum: state the leak in _pick_weighted's docstring (it currently only says "a weight function must not be able to make generation impossible") so WP11 does not read weight 0 as a vocabulary ban, and add a test pinning the current behaviour either way.

Scratch scripts in /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP5/ (a1_stream_identity.py, a2_probes.py, a3_partura_pick.py, a4_fake_test.py, a5_edges.py, a6_real_weights.py, a7_hook_rng.py, mutate.py, old_generator.py); nothing in either worktree was modified.

WHAT I VERIFIED MYSELF RATHER THAN TAKING ON TRUST

(b) Default-path identity, against the TRUE pre-WP5 code, not against another new generator. I extracted generator.py from the parent commit (`git show 6d14711:src/.../generator.py`), loaded it as a sibling module, and compared the real old class to the new one on 12 seeds x 7 parameter combos (defaults, max_depth=5, allow_boolean_ops, allow_resource_risk, include_lookahead, a ban set, max_retries=1/depth 2) using both `[e.key() for e in generate_population(40)]` and a random.Random subclass logging every (method, len) call: 0 mismatches, equal call sequences. Same for all five mutate_* plus crossover over 8 seeds x 12 trees: 0 mismatches. The implementer's claim holds.

Default fallback cannot spuriously raise: `is_valid_root(self._collapse_leaf(s))` is True for every one of the 26 root reducers, 6 field draws each, under all four vocabulary flag combinations — so the `tries == 1` branch always returns on its first candidate and GenerationExhausted is unreachable with no hook and no ban. Spec names are unique (244/244 with include_lookahead), so the name-keyed `weights` dict in __init__ cannot collapse two specs.

(d) Test quality, by mutation testing (mutate.py, 8 mutations, each a verbatim copy of the shipped method with one thing broken). Red as they should be: mutate_window reverted to is_valid_root; mutate_constant reverted; `_pick_weighted` inner draw made uniform; `_build` filling every leaf_slots slot. Survived all 27 tests: (1) `relaxed` without `_ban_ok` -> defect #1; (2) face mass = sum instead of mean -> no test pins face-balancing in the weighted path, folded into defect #2; (3) `acceptable()`'s order swapped so the hook runs before `_ban_ok` — the code is right and matches the design, but nothing pins the order or the "one_layer_keys computed only when a ban set exists" short-circuit; (4) the `self.daily_fields and` guard removed from `_gen` — all 27 new tests pass, BUT the full suite goes red at tests/test_mining.py::test_skip_kernels_reproduces_the_trajectory_until_the_first_refusal (1 failed, 794 passed), which compares two whole GPMiner runs key-for-key. So "the single most important guarantee in the design" is covered — by a pre-existing test, not by this file. Note that test_generate_population_identical_with_all_defaults_made_explicit and test_leaf_slots_and_daily_fields_both_empty_match_the_plain_population compare new-vs-new and therefore cannot detect any default-path regression; they are weak, not wrong, and the design asked for the first one verbatim.

(a) Design conformance, step by step: all 7 keywords with the design's names/defaults/order; all 7 attributes plus hook_rng and unaccepted_fallbacks; the hook_rng doc note; four of the five construction-time rejections exactly as specified (the fifth, "every op_weight key names a registered operator", exists only in the Mapping form — a pure callable has no keys, which is the ambiguity the implementer flagged, and the resolution they shipped is the right reading); `_ban_ok` + acceptable's order; the generate() fallback matching the design's pseudocode and its GenerationExhausted message verbatim; `_pick`'s uniform branch verbatim; the two mutation fixes with the escape hatch; mutate_operator untouched; the daily-leaf branch and the leaf_slots branch exactly as the design's snippets; GenerationExhausted in __all__. The only conformance break is `_pick_weighted`'s denominator (defect #2).

The three declared deviations are all sound. cs_bucket_rank really is absent from AlphaCube's registry (Partura-plugin-only), and cs_regres exercises the same mechanism. The op_weight Mapping form is additive — `self.op_weight` is always a callable after __init__, so WP7 can forward either shape. The all-zero tension is real and read correctly: the design does demand both a construction-time rejection for a pool-emptying weight table AND a uniform fallback for an all-zero draw, and those cannot both apply to the same value; splitting them (init check global, `_pick_weighted` fallback per-draw) is the only consistent resolution.

Not defects, but worth knowing. GenerationExhausted is a ValueError and gp.py's three `generator.generate()` call sites (gp.py:666, 680, 687) are unguarded, so with a ban set that nothing survives a mining run now dies instead of returning a banned tree — the design's deliberate change (b), explicitly accepted, and with 320 reachable minimal keys vs ban_top_n=2 per block it is not a practical risk. A post-construction op_weight returning +inf makes `random.choices` raise "Total of weights must be finite" (NaN and -inf are clamped to 0 safely); only reachable by reassigning op_weight after __init__ or by a stateful hook, which no design-sanctioned caller does. The ValueError wordings the implementer flagged as low-confidence are fine as shipped — WP7's step list does not string-match on them.
